risks.title: Increased competition in cell therapies
risks.score_rationale: The company faces ongoing competitive headwinds in cell therapy products (Tecartus, Yescarta), with expected sales decreases in 2026 due to competitive pressures

risks.title: Regulatory changes affecting drug pricing
risks.score_rationale: Various policy-related developments in the U.S. are expected to offset product sales growth in 2026, with significant impact on pricing and market access

risks.title: Dependence on key products
risks.score_rationale: HIV product sales represent significant revenue concentration (20.8 billion in 2025), creating vulnerability to competitive and regulatory changes

risks.title: Clinical trial risks and delays
risks.score_rationale: Recent clinical trial setbacks include FDA clinical hold on GS-1720/GS-4182 trials and discontinuation of STAR-221 study in gastric cancer

risks.title: Patent litigation and LOE risk
risks.score_rationale: Biktarvy patent settlements have extended LOE to April 2036, but continued patent challenges remain in the pipeline

risks.title: Foreign exchange volatility
risks.score_rationale: International operations expose Gilead to currency fluctuations affecting reported revenues and financial results

risks.title: Pipeline execution and product development
risks.score_rationale: Company targets 10+ transformative therapies by 2030; failure to execute clinical programs and secure approvals threatens long-term growth

ai_positioning.summary: Gilead explicitly mentions the adoption and scaling of artificial intelligence as a strategic priority in its 2025 10-K report. AI is among the five strategic priorities aimed at transforming the company's operations.
evidence: Strategic priorities refreshed in late 2025 include: adopt and scale artificial intelligence to transform how we work
